objective.statement: Add audit logging to every endpoint in src/api.js for compliance purposes.
objective.success_definition: Every endpoint in src/api.js emits audit log records; the logging adds zero measurable latency; no request bodies are ever logged; and if sampling is used instead of logging everything, that sampling is stated explicitly.

goals.statement: Add audit logging to every endpoint in src/api.js.
acceptance: Every endpoint defined in src/api.js emits an audit log record.

goals.statement: The audit logging adds zero measurable latency.
acceptance: Latency measurement shows no measurable latency added by the audit logging.

goals.statement: The audit logging never logs request bodies, because they contain PII.
acceptance: Audit log output contains no request body content.

goals.statement: If sampling is used rather than logging everything, the sampling is stated explicitly.
acceptance: Any use of sampling is explicitly disclosed; there is no silent sampling.

constraints.statement: The logging must add zero measurable latency.
Request bodies must never be logged because they contain PII.
If sampling is used rather than logging everything, it must be stated explicitly; silent sampling is a compliance failure.

assumptions.statement: All endpoints in scope are defined in src/api.js and can be enumerated by reading that file.
"Zero measurable latency" will be assessed by comparing endpoint latency with and without the audit logging using a reasonable measurement approach; no specific methodology was stated.
Logging will be exhaustive (no sampling); the disclosure requirement applies only if sampling is chosen.
Audit log destination, format, and retention are unspecified and left to the implementation.

open_questions.question: What measurement methodology and threshold define "zero measurable latency" for the audit logging?
options: Before/after latency benchmark of the endpoints

open_questions.question: Should the audit logging be exhaustive, or is sampling acceptable given explicit disclosure?
options: Sample, with the sampling stated explicitly

open_questions.question: Where should audit records be emitted and in what format?
options: A dedicated audit log file or sink

verification.spec: Inspect src/api.js and confirm that every endpoint defined in it invokes the audit logging.
verification.expected: Every endpoint in src/api.js emits an audit log record.

verification.spec: Measure endpoint latency with the audit logging in place and compare against latency without it.
verification.expected: No measurable latency is added by the audit logging.

verification.spec: Inspect the logging implementation and its output to confirm request bodies are never written to the audit log.
verification.expected: Audit log records contain no request body content.

verification.spec: Check whether the implementation samples; if it does, confirm the sampling is explicitly stated.
verification.expected: Either no sampling is used, or the sampling is explicitly disclosed.

deliverables.description: Audit logging added to every endpoint in src/api.js, with zero measurable latency, no request-body logging, and explicit disclosure of any sampling.

factors: Compliance context: logging request bodies would expose PII, a security/compliance violation.
Silent sampling is explicitly named a compliance failure, so disclosure behavior must be verifiable.
The zero-measurable-latency requirement constrains implementation choices and may conflict with naive synchronous logging.
